summary: Read-only local review completed against control commit 0bb19618; inspected tools match that commit. The original request/plan pins verify and derive J-f9edc8f6f35dde13. Journal contains zero production controllers/jobs. Original P1 status: (1) partially resolved: development NEEDS_REPAIR now invokes workload-source repair, independent review, rejected-repair rework and accepted reentry; offline/control-code repair remains unsupported. (2) partially resolved: initial-review, failed-analysis, failed-decision and source-preparation replacements preserve predecessors and charges, and consumers select active attempts; automatic exception dispatch remains absent. (3) partially resolved: platform evidence now reaches delivery, final and terminal audits, removing the unconditional UNKNOWN barrier, but complete wait coverage and actual deployment/handoff remain unproven. Accepted revision reentry releases the writer lock and starts a fresh interpreter, checking reviewed code, commit, controller identity, cursor, Store, old-process death and reservation. Its one-shot claim correctly refuses blind replay. Subsequent existing-job recovery must use the ordinary controller entry: register preserves the revised identity/cursor, run_job reuses the submission claim, and submit never resubmits it. The revision-resume entry is deliberately not that recovery route: its idle guard rejects active jobs and its consumed claim cannot be retried. These are static conclusions, not production recovery acceptance. No repository/Journal/Store edits, GPU queries, simulation, training, approvals or agents were used. One in-memory coverage counterexample was evaluated; fixture reports were inspected, not rerun. CPU results, this review and future controller deployment do not constitute scientific completion.
next_plan: Implement and independently review only the baseline exception handoff and complete wait-coverage corrections below; preserve all previous failures and charges. Verify revision-start versus ordinary existing-job recovery with bounded CPU cases, without building a generic scheduler. Resolve the actual platform auto-continuation handoff, deploy one detached controller under the existing lock with durable logs and an explicit normal-recovery entry, verify ownership/STOP/event-trigger behavior, then end the launching model turn. After real baseline closure and analysis, follow evidence into workload repair, baseline-sufficient validation or candidate development; implement control/offline/confirmation/final repair transitions only when their events require them. Preserve three-stream confirmation or the truthful zero-training alternative, unseen holdout rules, genuine videos, resource/model audits and final independent acceptance. No repeated generic permission request is needed for already authorized task work.
must_fix: P1 — Before autonomous baseline deployment: connect baseline failures to a bounded repair handoff. tools/r6_controller.py:269-278 invokes FIRST_JOB, but :416-426 only saves INCOMPLETE_EXCEPTION and raises. tools/r6_start_baseline.py:37-53, tools/r6_finalize_job.py:47-61,77-103 and tools/r6_source_preparation.py:296-321 consume existing active attempts; they do not create a repaired successor when the selected attempt fails. The replacement primitives are real, but their existence does not complete autonomous recovery. Add a durable event keyed to the exact failed phase/receipt and a bounded authorized repair disposition that invokes the existing replacement registration after cleanup and evidence reconciliation. STOP, ambiguous ownership and missing receipts must remain fail-closed. This needs only the initial-review/closed-baseline-analysis/decision boundary, not every future failure route or a generic scheduling framework.

P1 — Before first baseline evidence capture: distinguish observed waiter segments from complete job-wait coverage. tools/r6_submit.py:175-191 submits before tools/r6_audited_job_handoff.py:33 starts its audit; tools/r6_wait_audit.py:21-38 starts at the current observation time. A crash after submission but before that first record can therefore restart with a fresh, apparently complete audit and omit earlier live waiting. tools/r6_platform_wait.py:116-134 checks supplied segments but never compares their union with authoritative job start/closure boundaries or validates coverage between segments; tools/r6_delivery_evidence.py:63-76 can promote them to a zero-call result. An in-memory counterexample with windows [100,110] and [190,200] and a root turn [120,180] returns platform_inactivity_proven=true; this demonstrates the validator limitation, not a production occurrence. Persist the required coverage start before submission effects, bind it to exact job/process lifecycle evidence, and require complete interval coverage or explicitly retain UNKNOWN. Also bind trace completeness to a supported capture/flush or writer-health boundary: reading a stale, newline-complete log at a later wall-clock time is not by itself proof of coverage through that time. Preserve existing prefix, ownership, late-append and restart-gap rejection checks.

P1 — Deployment/platform prerequisite: establish a real detached handoff before new dispatch. tools/r6_platform_wait.py:103-113 intentionally rejects an open root turn; tools/r6_run_job.py:56-57 and tools/r6_submit.py:104-105,124 invoke it. These checks observe platform activity and cannot disable automatic Goal continuation. tools/r6_controller_revision.py:192-198 starts a fresh child but does not establish detached service ownership or a platform handoff. Arrange the supported platform transition away from automatic inference, start the single local controller through existing tmux/service facilities, record PID/starttime/boot identity, lock, logs and recovery command, and perform bounded handoff checks before ending the launch turn. Have a bounded local gate handle the handoff transition rather than losing the controller to the expected open-turn exception. Do not bypass preflight or claim zero-model production waiting while automatic continuation remains active. Recovered sandbox access and already provisioned first-baseline volumes are not current administrator blockers.

P2 — Downstream, when an analysis replacement is needed: honor its validated timeout during ordinary controller reentry. tools/r6_analysis_repair.py:75-107 permits a changed timeout as a legitimate repaired input, but tools/r6_finalize_job.py:38,50-58 compares the active replacement against the caller's default timeout_seconds=3600; finish_and_decide at :115 supplies no override. A valid replacement with a different timeout therefore fails FINALIZE_ANALYSIS_BINDING instead of resuming. Select the validated active request's bounded execution settings, or propagate its exact repaired settings through the controller. Test registration followed by the normal finalizer/controller entry, not only direct helper handoff. This does not block a fresh baseline using the default analysis settings.

P2 — Downstream, event-triggered before the affected phase resumes: offline/control-code and frozen-phase repair remain unfinished. tools/r6_source_preparation.py:150-154 explicitly requires PREPARATION_INCOMPLETE for offline-only or controller changes, and :204 rejects that result; tools/r6_source_repair.py:23-24 restricts writable scope. The accepted-revision mechanism at tools/r6_controller_revision.py:99-173 and tools/r6_controller_resume.py:22-82 reviews/resumes an already supplied repair, but does not produce one. tools/r6_controller.py:241-246 parks frozen-phase repair and :220-221,266-268 parks final MUST_FIX. Preserve those protections and add only the concrete repair writer/disposition required by actual evidence, followed by exact review and fresh-process reentry where needed. For a crash after a resume claim, use ordinary exact-job recovery under the same writer lock; never clear or replay that claim. Confirmation and post-holdout repair need separate accepted inputs and contamination handling, not inherited approval. These phase-specific implementations can be deferred beyond the first baseline once the bounded failure handoff exists.
